doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Piano influences: Waller, Teddy Wilson and Bud Powell
summary: Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson first, later bebop and Bud Powell; he later traveled with Wilson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Tell us about some of your influences, some of your keyboard influences.

Well at the beginning you know since it happened when I was eleven, twelve years old taking those piano lessons, the music that appealed to me most then was the pianists Fats Waller and Teddy Wilson. Really different kinds of pianists but I loved them both. They were both great. Particularly Teddy. I even tried to imitate him, like get his records and try to play like him you know. And many years passed and I was able to meet him and we even traveled together on two different trips — one over in Russia for six weeks, and then later with Buddy Rich, I was with Buddy and he had his own trio and I got to know him which was a big thrill for me. So anyhow those were my first influences. Then later, after World War II I got in with the beboppers.
Who was your favorite bebop artist on keyboard?
Bud Powell. By far, yeah. He was outstanding. To me there was nobody like Bud Powell. He was so exciting. Yeah.
